title: One terminal vocabulary for SprintContract, and the rank-aware channel join
description: Two engines pick different words from the same enum for the same outcome — runSprintCycle writes "passed", PGE's sprint_exit writes "completed" — and five production readers filter for only one of them, so both MCP sprint tools return empty against a corpus of 250 contracts holding zero "passed". Standardise the word, give the readers a shared predicate so a third word cannot silently break them again, and replace the channel reducer's canonical-order duplicate resolution with the rank-aware join already shipping beside it. Closes two of the four conformance divergences.

resolvedClarifications.answer: Standardise on "completed", and add a shared isSettled() predicate for readers. The ts engine's runSprintCycle changes to write "completed"; PGE already does. Rationale: "completed" matches the on-disk majority (218 of 250 committed contracts), so nothing already written goes stale, and updateContractStatus (sprint-contract.ts:216-219) already treats it as terminal. A predicate alone was rejected because it fixes the readers without making the two engines agree, which leaves the `contracts` divergence open.

Add version?: number to SprintContractSchema. versionRank (reducers.ts:348-359) already reads a `version` number, so no reducer logic is invented. Optional, so all 250 existing contracts stay valid. Rejected: riding as an unknown key, because loadContract parses through a non-strict schema that strips unknown keys, so the discriminator would vanish on any load round-trip.

Migrate the four contracts carrying "pending" (all from spec-20260604-docs-correction) to a legal status, and add a test asserting no committed contract carries a status outside ContractStatusSchema — so this class of drift is caught rather than accumulating.

updatedAt cannot serve as the discriminator even though versionRank already reads it: the replay harness runs on a fixed clock, so the seeded and settled copies stamp identically and the comparison falls through to the canonical-order tiebreak — exactly the defect being fixed. Established by the planner during scoping.

approvalEvidence: src/orchestrator/workflow/resume-cursor.ts:22 (already reads BOTH — the shape isSettled should take)
src/contracts/sprint-contract.ts:38-49 (ContractStatusSchema enum), :216-219 (updateContractStatus already treats passed|failed|completed as terminal)
src/pge/registry/reducers.ts:187 (mergeEntries resolves duplicates by joinByCanonicalOrder — the defect)
src/pge/registry/reducers.ts:348-367 (versionRank and rankIsGreater already exist and already read `version` then `updatedAt`)
.bober/contracts/*.json measured on main: 218 completed, 28 proposed, 4 pending, 0 passed

assumptions: MEASURED on main: the 250 committed contracts hold 218 "completed", 28 "proposed", 4 "pending" and ZERO "passed". Both MCP sprint tools filter status === "passed" (mcp/tools/sprint.ts:147, mcp/tools/eval.ts:139) and therefore return empty today. So do the two CLI equivalents (cli/commands/sprint.ts:160, cli/commands/eval.ts:127) and the history counter (state/history.ts:193).

"pending" is not a member of ContractStatusSchema (contracts/sprint-contract.ts:38-49), so four committed contracts carry a status the schema does not permit. All four belong to spec-20260604-docs-correction.

The two writers disagree: runSprintCycle writes "passed" (orchestrator/pipeline.ts:589), PGE's sprint_exit writes "completed" (pge/nodes/sprint-review.ts:203). This is a pre-existing ambiguity the conformance harness surfaced, not one PGE introduced.

A shared predicate is already half-present: orchestrator/workflow/resume-cursor.ts:22 filters on BOTH words, and updateContractStatus (contracts/sprint-contract.ts:216-219) already treats passed|failed|completed as terminal. isSettled() should generalise what those two already do.

mergeEntries resolves a duplicate id by joinByCanonicalOrder (pge/registry/reducers.ts:187). Every settled status sorts before the seeded "proposed" under canonical order, so the channel keeps the PLANNED copy — which is why a pge run reports a contract still marked "proposed" inside completedSprints.

versionRank (reducers.ts:348-359) and rankIsGreater (:361-367) ALREADY EXIST and already rank by `version` number, then `updatedAt`, then canonical JSON. They are used by keepHighestRanked for the spec and verdict channels. Switching mergeEntries to rankIsGreater therefore invents no new ranking logic.
The same canonical-order resolution is the latent defect in lastWriteWinsByKey (reducers.ts around :288-297) where attempts:10 sorts below attempts:9. The rank-aware join fixes both call sites.

updatedAt cannot be the discriminator: the replay harness uses a fixed clock, so the seeded and settled copies stamp identically and rankIsGreater falls through to canonical order — reproducing the defect. A monotone `version` written at sprint_exit is required for replay stability.

Persistence asymmetry: saveContract writes the raw object (state/sprint-state.ts) while loadContract parses through a NON-STRICT schema that strips unknown keys. So a discriminator lands on disk regardless; schema membership decides only whether it survives a load round-trip.

CERTAIN BLAST RADIUS: the two-directional pins in orchestrator/workflow/conformance.engines.test.ts (both the divergence-set list and the per-field records) and oracle-retention.test.ts fail when a divergence is FIXED as well as when one is added. pge/nodes/sprint-evaluate.test.ts pins the current "completed" write. Each must be edited deliberately, in the same commit as the docs/pge-graph.md disposition it changes.

The golden dataset holds 6 enforcement:"replay" cases against a floor of 5 (GOLDEN_MIN_REPLAY_CASES) — zero slack. Any change to what a contract's status or version field holds moves recorded artifacts and forces a re-capture.

The just-completed spec-20260812-pge-real-workload-errors established the discipline this spec inherits: caps and ceilings pinned as functions of measured data, negative controls that scale with the dataset, and every change carrying its own blast radius rather than deferring it to a later sprint.
outOfScope: Closing the `history` or `audits` conformance divergences. Both are recommended for permanent acceptance on architectural grounds — there is no curator node to emit a start/complete pair from, and five of eight checkpoint ids sit inside the fan-out region where HITL is a frozen ADR-6 error.
Flipping config.pipeline.engine to "pge". The default stays "ts" and oracle-retention.test.ts stays green throughout.
Re-specifying the conformance bar. This spec closes two divergences; deciding what the remaining bar should be is a separate, stated decision.
Option B success semantics (success:false on a fail-closed refusal).
Executing the commit or finalize nodes under a durable checkpoint mechanism.
Adding a golden case to reach critique and rework_route (worth ~40/44 coverage, recorded as a follow-up by the previous spec).
Renaming or restructuring ContractStatusSchema beyond what D3 requires.
Any change to how the evaluator decides pass or fail. This spec changes the WORD recorded for an outcome, never the outcome itself.

features.title: A shared settled-status predicate, and the MCP tools work again
features.description: Five production readers each hardcode one of two words. Give them one predicate, and the live bug — both MCP sprint tools returning empty against a 250-contract corpus — closes immediately.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: A single exported predicate decides whether a contract's status is terminal, and it generalises what updateContractStatus (sprint-contract.ts:216-219) and resume-cursor.ts:22 already do independently.

AC2: Every production reader that hardcoded status === "passed" or status === "completed" for a terminal check uses the predicate instead — mcp/tools/sprint.ts, mcp/tools/eval.ts, cli/commands/sprint.ts, cli/commands/eval.ts, state/history.ts.
AC3: A test drives both MCP sprint tools against the committed 250-contract corpus and asserts a NON-EMPTY settled list — the live bug, closed and pinned.
AC4: A test asserts no production module outside the predicate compares a contract status to a status literal for a terminal check, so a sixth reader cannot reintroduce the bug.

features.title: No contract carries a status the schema forbids
features.description: Four committed contracts carry "pending", which ContractStatusSchema does not permit. Migrate them and add the guard that would have caught it.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: The four contracts from spec-20260604-docs-correction carrying "pending" are migrated to a legal status, with the chosen value justified in the commit.
AC2: A test reads every committed contract and asserts its status parses against ContractStatusSchema; it fails if any file carries a value outside the enum.
AC3: The test is proven to bite by mutation — introducing an illegal status in a temp copy fails it.

features.title: A monotone discriminator that survives replay
features.description: appendById keeps the seeded copy over the settled one because canonical order puts every settled status first. Give the contract a version the existing rank-aware join can read, and write it replay-stably.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: SprintContractSchema declares version?: number, optional so all 250 committed contracts stay valid.
AC2: sprint_exit writes a monotone version, and the value is REPLAY-STABLE — a replayed run produces the same version as the recorded run, proven by a golden case rather than argued.
AC3: A test asserts the settled copy outranks the seeded one under versionRank, and that the ordering does not depend on updatedAt (which a fixed clock makes identical).
AC4: A round-trip test proves the version survives saveContract followed by loadContract — the asymmetry that made the unknown-key option unworkable.

features.title: The channel join is rank-aware, and pipelineResult converges
features.description: Replace mergeEntries' canonical-order duplicate resolution with the rank-aware join already shipping beside it, which also fixes the latent attempts-ordering defect in lastWriteWinsByKey.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: mergeEntries resolves a duplicate id with rankIsGreater rather than joinByCanonicalOrder, and no new ranking logic is introduced — versionRank and rankIsGreater are reused as they ship.
AC2: A test proves the settled contract now outranks the seeded "proposed" one, so a pge run no longer reports a contract still marked "proposed" inside completedSprints.
AC3: The latent lastWriteWinsByKey defect is fixed and pinned: attempts:10 must outrank attempts:9, which canonical order got backwards.
AC4: Order-invariance is preserved — the property appendById exists for. A test asserts the merge result is identical regardless of the order the containers arrive in.

AC5: The `pipelineResult` conformance divergence is closed, and the two-directional pin in conformance.engines.test.ts is edited DELIBERATELY in the same commit as the docs/pge-graph.md disposition it changes.

features.title: Both engines write the same word, and contracts converges
features.description: The ts engine changes to write "completed", matching PGE and the on-disk majority. This is the change that makes the two engines agree about what happened.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: runSprintCycle writes "completed" where it wrote "passed", and every ts-side reader of that write follows.

AC2: The `contracts` conformance divergence is closed — the status delta is gone, and the two remaining field deltas (evaluatorFeedback, generatorNotes) are either closed or recorded with a stated reason.
AC3: pge/nodes/sprint-evaluate.test.ts, which pins the current write, is edited deliberately rather than incidentally.
AC4: The six replay golden cases are re-captured and the diff is verified confined to the status word, the version field and their direct consequences — anything else moving is a stop condition.
AC5: The replay count stays at or above GOLDEN_MIN_REPLAY_CASES and no case is relabelled from replay to integrity.

features.title: The convergence record
features.description: State honestly what the divergence set is now, what closing the rest would take, and what a default flip would still require. A spec that closes two divergences should say so in the place the last one recorded them.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: conformance.engines.test.ts pins the divergence set to exactly what a real run now produces, with the per-field records updated to match, and still fails in BOTH directions.
AC2: docs/pge-graph.md's engine-migration disposition records which divergences closed, which remain, and why the remaining ones are recommended for permanent acceptance.
AC3: oracle-retention.test.ts still asserts the default is "ts" and TsPipelineEngine is still both selected and the fallback — this spec does not flip anything.
AC4: The document states plainly what a flip would still require beyond this spec, so nobody reads two closed divergences as a green light.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: No gate may be weakened to make this spec green. Every two-directional pin edited must still fail in both directions afterwards.
nonFunctionalRequirements.verificationMethod: Each edited pin is mutation-tested in both directions by the evaluator, and the negative controls in the golden suite are re-verified to still bite at the current case count.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: Order-invariance of the channel reducers is preserved. appendById exists to be order-invariant under concurrency and must remain so.
nonFunctionalRequirements.verificationMethod: A test merges the same containers in several different orders and asserts an identical result.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The version discriminator must be replay-stable. A value derived from wall-clock time or run order would make every golden case irreproducible.
nonFunctionalRequirements.verificationMethod: A captured golden case replays byte-identically, and a test asserts the version does not vary between two runs over the same input.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The terminal-status decision lives in exactly one place. A sixth reader must not be able to reintroduce the bug by hardcoding a literal.
nonFunctionalRequirements.verificationMethod: A test scans production modules for status-literal comparisons used as terminal checks and fails on any outside the predicate.

techNotes.dataModel: SprintContract gains an optional monotone `version: number`. ContractStatusSchema is unchanged in membership; what changes is which member the ts engine writes. The sprintContracts channel keeps appendById, but its duplicate resolution moves from joinByCanonicalOrder to the rank-aware rankIsGreater that already ships in the same module.
techNotes.existingPatterns: Reuse rather than invent: versionRank and rankIsGreater already exist and already read `version`. Generalise resume-cursor.ts:22 and updateContractStatus rather than writing a third terminal-status rule. Follow the previous spec's discipline — pin claims two-directionally, prove every gate bites by mutation, and make each change carry its own golden blast radius in its own sprint.

metadata.riskNotes: Lower risk than its predecessor: no topology change, no new channel, no frozen-surface revision. The risk concentrates in two places — the deliberate edits to two-directional conformance pins, where the danger is editing one incidentally rather than deliberately, and the replay-stability of the version discriminator, where a wall-clock-derived value would silently make every golden case irreproducible. Both are addressed by dedicated criteria rather than left to care.
